Binding site is a coarse coordination label (metal neighbours of the closest adsorbate atom within +0.45 Å of the shortest contact: 1→atop, 2→bridge, ≥3→hollow). For weakly physisorbed alkanes the site is indicative only; the bond distance and contact pair are the robust metrics.
Geometry coverage: all 415 systems now have images on both sides. 67 MLIP slots use the exact published base GOAD image and its archived contact distance because an Omni image is unavailable; the captions identify this variant. Coordination sites and original coordinates for these base records are not archived here. These additions provide structural context; they do not change the geometries or values associated with the energy tables. Base-image and contact provenance.
Single-point adsorption energies: 1003 functional results across 287 of the 415 systems below; 418 original published results, 314 Kestrel results, 233 Perlmutter results and 38 results using shared stored references; cluster additions use relaxed references.

Completed results outside the review range: 186 additional relaxed values are shown in amber with a dagger (†). They passed convergence and composition checks but exceed |Eads| = 5 eV; they are not screened benchmark values. They and any derived differences are excluded from the energy-figure statistics. Displayed relaxed results requiring energy review. Positive absolute total energies are allowed; their sign does not determine convergence or reference compatibility.
Project reference policy: POTCAR variants such as Ag and Ag_pv are treated as equivalent for filtering. Potential identity differences do not exclude a result; the original potential names remain in the audit. No energy offset or correction is applied.
Previously published values preserved: 470 additional relaxed energies and their published ML differences are retained when the current audit cannot supply a replacement. These are historical results, not newly screened results. Hover over an energy or dash for its provenance and current audit findings; audit findings do not replace published energies. A dash in a relaxed DFT cell means no retained published value or completed, composition-matched result is available. Published relaxed-energy snapshot. Existing structure images are from the earlier geometry extraction; added Kestrel images carry their own functional and source audit. Geometry metrics retain the earlier extraction, and an image does not imply a new adsorption-energy result; historical single-point values are retained; new Kestrel results have a separate source audit. Screened relaxed energies · Full extraction and status report.
All table energies are in eV; Δ = Eads(ML) − Eads(DFT). Eads = E(slab + molecule) − E(slab) − E(molecule). The single-point columns compare energies evaluated without further geometry relaxation; the images show relaxed structures. The combined column uses the ML and DFT values displayed in the relaxed comparison. A dash means a required input is unavailable. Download the displayed single-point energies · Full single-point dataset.
Kestrel single-point convention: Eads(SPE) = E(complex, NSW=0) − E(relaxed slab) − E(relaxed molecule). New entries require completed, electronically converged single-point complexes and converged relaxed references with matching functional and composition, using the existing |Eads| ≤ 5 eV review screen.
Combined column: Eads(ML) − Eads(SPE) − Eads(DFT, relaxed). It uses the displayed relaxed-comparison inputs and the full-precision SPE value; all three must be available. Published SPE energies and single-point Δ values are preserved; their original ML references remain in the download. New single-point Δ values use the displayed relaxed-comparison ML value.

These calculations use the original ML POSCAR, verified against the recorded staging hashes, with NSW=0. POTCAR variants follow the existing project policy; no scaling, offsets or sign-based rejection is applied. Missing, incomplete and reference-limited results remain in the audit; the SPE batch is still in progress at this snapshot.

Energy differences: method residual and relaxation

(ML − relaxed DFT) = (ML − SPE) + (SPE − relaxed DFT). All terms here are adsorption energies in eV. Subtracting the same-geometry residual from the total leaves (ML − relaxed DFT) − (ML − SPE) = SPE − relaxed DFT, not ML − relaxed DFT − SPE.

Interpretation: ML − SPE measures a same-geometry model discrepancy only when the ML and SPE structures and adsorption-reference conventions match. It includes ML approximation error, functional differences and reference offsets; it is not a pure functional correction. SPE − relaxed DFT is a relaxation contribution only with compatible references, potentials, numerical settings and a linked initial/final geometry. It is not a functional-independent "true error".

Current evidence is descriptive: 756 complete ML/SPE/relaxed triples across 273 exact surface/molecule pairs out of 1003 displayed SPE entries. Missing inputs are omitted, never treated as zero. 127 rows with explicitly marked energy-review values are excluded from these paired statistics; the tables retain their values. All panels use the same triples within each functional. Historical and audited results are mixed; geometry identity and cross-run reference compatibility have not been established. Kestrel SPE values currently subtract relaxed molecule/slab references; the newly submitted reference SPE jobs are not included. POTCAR variants were allowed by the existing publication policy, which does not establish physical reference equivalence. The existing energy screen can bias these distributions.

One ML value is used consistently per row: the displayed relaxed-comparison ML energy. Historical SPE differences sometimes used another ML reference; those published differences remain unchanged and are not used in these plots. Displayed ML/relaxed precision limits the derived differences. Formate and formic acid remain separate.

Functional sensitivity on a common cohort

130 systems have SPE values for all four functionals; ML and relaxed energies are not required for this panel. PBE+D3: -0.338 eV mean (-0.297 median); r2SCAN: -0.097 eV mean (-0.053 median); BEEF-vdW: -0.321 eV mean (-0.253 median). Negative shifts mean stronger adsorption than PBE. Pairing removes system-composition imbalance, but does not prove identical geometry or settings. These are observed method/reference shifts, not isolated exchange-correlation effects or an accuracy ranking.

Cancellation versus reinforcement

Each point is an exact surface/molecule/functional triple. Its x + y value is the total ML−relaxed discrepancy. Opposite signs cancel; equal signs reinforce. A negative gap below −0.01 eV occurs in 28 triples: these require provenance/geometry review, not clipping. For genuinely matched calculations relaxed to a lower energy with identical references, the gap should be nonnegative.

Legacy-column warning: the retained ML − SPE − DFT (relaxed) column is literal arithmetic, not an error decomposition or a corrected physical error. It is excluded from this analysis.

Molecule notation: DME = CH3OCH3 (dimethyl ether); ethanol = CH3CH2OH = C2H5OH; methanol = CH3OH; acetaldehyde = CH3CHO; acetic acid = CH3COOH; formaldehyde = H2CO; formic acid = HCOOH. Names, condensed formulas and subscript digits work in the search box. Ethanol and DME remain distinct despite both having formula C2H6O; formate and formic acid, and propanol and isopropanol, also remain distinct.
Converged binding energies are displayed even outside the ±5 eV review range, with amber review markers. Missing or failed references and slab-size mismatches are separate from unusual energy magnitudes. Notation equivalences · Directory-to-page name audit · DME energy and reference audit.
A blank binding energy can still have a converged complex. Binding energies require compatible complex, clean-slab and gas-molecule results. Ag111–DME PBE has completed relaxed and SPE complexes, but its gas reference is unfinished and its standard Perlmutter slab has the wrong atom count. Size-specific Kestrel slabs are now used through the shared-reference audit; Ag111–DME BEEF-vdW is available with an energy-review marker.
